text: Clinical Reviewer's Comment: The demographic and disease characteristics, in terms of age, sex, race, ethnicity, and mean baseline body weight, were similar across the two treatment arms, EU-Stelara and CT-P43, for Treatment Period I (TP1) and for Treatment Period II (TP2).

The phase 3 clinical study, Study CT-P43 3.1, provides the main comparative data for the safety review. During TP1, the overall rate of TEAEs was higher for the CT-P43 treatment group (37.1% - 155 events in 95 subjects), compared to the EU-Stelara treatment group (29.6% - 108 events in 75 subjects) (Table 20). The overall rates of SAEs were similar 1.6% (4 subjects) for the CT-P43 treatment and 1.6% (4 subjects) for the EU-Stelara treatment groups. No subjects discontinued treatment due to an AE during TP1.

During TP2, TEAEs were reported in 34.0% (144 events in 86 subjects) for the CT-P43 maintenance, in 40.8% (78 events in 51 subjects) for the EU-Stelara maintenance and in 41.9% (95 events in 52 subjects) for the Switched to CT-P43 treatment groups. The overall rates of SAEs were similar in the CT-P43 maintenance, EU-Stelara maintenance (2.4%), and Switched to CT-P43 (1.6%) groups. However, slightly more subjects discontinued due to an AE in the CT-P43 maintenance group (2.0%) compared to the EU-Stelara maintenance (0.8%) and Switched to CT-P43 (TP2) (0.8%) groups (Table 36). The details for the discontinuations are discussed further in the section Dropouts and Discontinuations below.
